Definition: from the same as G257; to tread out grain:--thresh, tread out the corn.
BiblicalUsage: To tread out grain, to thresh, and Paul uses it three times to make the same point from the law: Thou shalt not muzzle the mouth of the ox that treadeth out the corn. The ox eats while it works, and Paul says the labourer in the gospel is worthy of his hire, and the elder who rules well is worthy of double honour.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for threshing carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the argument built on it, that the ox is not muzzled and neither is the preacher.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
